inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report note 26 (reconciliation of loss to OCF): employee share scheme expense NZ$34,709 (FY25: NZ$140,843). No net-share-settlement taxes. The Metrics.csv StockBasedComp column (853,428 / 394,051) is the share-based payments RESERVE balance, not the annual expense -- do not use it.
inputs.buyback_note: Never repurchased a share; the flat count is a modelling convention. The company is a serial ISSUER: 32.5m shares (25% of the register) issued in FY26 alone.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 163,605,272 ordinary shares on issue per NZX (2026-09-18; ties to 163,361,489 at 31-Mar-2026 in FY26 AR note 18 + 243,783 options exercised per Capital Change Notice 19-Aug-2026) + 533,216 remaining options = 164,138,488. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; the negative early-year FCFs are discounted as if funded at fair value -- see notes on the funding gap for what a raise at the current price does to this figure.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-18T03:47:52Z (NZX last trade 15:47:51 NZST, regular session; Yahoo regularMarketTime)
inputs.balance_sheet_source: FY26 Annual Report (audited, auditor's report dated 29-May-2026, re-lodged 17-Jul-2026), notes 10, 16, 17, 18
inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built cost of equity = WACC (no material debt): NZ 10y govt ~4.5% + 5.5% ERP x beta 1.5 (loss-making micro-cap SaaS) = 12.75%, plus ~1.25pp illiquidity/size premium (NZ$19m market cap, sub-NZ$50k daily turnover) = 14.0%. Cross-check: the company's own FY26 impairment test uses a 17.8% PRE-tax discount rate (FY25: 17.0%), i.e. ~13-14% post-tax. Same 14% in all three scenarios; survival, execution and dilution risk are charged in the scenario flows and in the 30% bear weight, not stacked into the rate (owner-fcf.md s7f).
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods SKILL routing row 1: operating SaaS company), built as a staged PATH-TO-PROFITABILITY on a 10-year explicit horizon with component margins. TradeWindow is loss-making (six consecutive years) so a trailing or mid-cycle FCF multiple would be meaningless; the engine handles this because the early years carry negative owner FCF that is discounted like any other flow and the terminal value is floored at zero. The alternative routes were considered and rejected: the distressed/asset-waterfall model does not fit a company with NZ$4.2m cash, 90% retention and 17% ARR growth; a pure ARR-multiple would import a peer multiple for a business with no demonstrated path to positive FCF -- it is reported as a sanity memo only (sanity_check.ev_arr).

BASE YEAR: FY2026A (year ended 31-Mar-2026, audited) taken from the FY26 Annual Report downloaded from NZX for this build; it post-dates the Metrics.csv, whose last audited row is FY2025. inputs.last_fcf is the FY2026 owner FCF (-2.111); the FY2025 audited pair is retained as last_fcf_fy2025_audited (-1.849) for auditability.

OWNER FCF FY2026: reported FCF -2.010 (OCF -1.308 less PPE 0.042 less capitalised development 0.661) minus SBC 0.035 minus interest income 0.020 minus lease cash 0.047 = -2.111. Interest income is stripped because net cash (3.7m) is added back in the bridge.

EBITDA DRIVER IS PRE-SBC. The company's headline EBITDA (-1.242m, -12.9%) is after the SBC expense; ebitda_margin_path starts from the pre-SBC -12.6% and SBC is then charged explicitly at ~1% of revenue. SBC is small at TradeWindow (0.4% of FY26 revenue, 1.8% FY25); 1.0% is carried forward to allow for LTI grants to the new CEO.

LEASES: treatment (B) -- lease cash (principal 0.044 + interest 0.003 in FY26, 0.5% of revenue) is charged inside the flows and the NZ$6.6k lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A of 7% is ex-ROU (ROU depreciation is immaterial) and only matters through the tax line.

NET DEBT: 'no bank debt' is true (ASB loan repaid Dec-2025) but NZ$0.454m of interest-bearing debt remains: MBIE/Callaghan R&D loan 0.285 (3%, due 2030) + IQumulate insurance premium funding 0.169 (repaid by 30-Jun-2026). Both deducted. Net cash = 4.190 - 0.454 = 3.736m at 31-Mar-2026. The FY26 investor presentation reports average monthly cash outflow of NZ$184k ex-raises, so by mid-September 2026 cash is likely ~NZ$3.0m -- the bridge uses the audited March figure and is therefore ~0.7m (NZ$0.004/share) generous.

CASH TAX: NZ$39.1m of unrecognised tax losses (note 9) so cash tax is zero through year 6; ramped 10/20/28% in years 7-10 rather than sheltered in perpetuity, because the 25% register turnover in FY26 and any future raises put NZ shareholder-continuity at risk. Bear case never earns taxable profit so its rate is zero throughout. Note the NZ$1.036m of R&D tax losses previously cashed out is a contingent CLAWBACK on a change of control or IP disposal (note 9) -- not modelled, would reduce any takeout value.

CAPEX includes capitalised development: FY27 FreightAI spend guided at NZ$1.5m (vs NZ$0.66m capitalised in FY26) with full platform rollout ~Sept-2027, so capex_pct_path is 15% in year 1 falling to 5.5% mature. Capitalisation keeps this spend OUT of the company's EBITDA; the model charges it in full as capex.

WORKING CAPITAL is an OUTFLOW on growth (wc_capture -5%): receivables grow faster than contract liabilities (FY26 net -0.084m on +1.58m revenue growth; FY25 -0.157m on +1.85m). Not a prepaid-subscription business at the cash level.

GOING CONCERN: the FY26 audit opinion (29-May-2026, re-lodged 17-Jul-2026 with an administrative correction) STILL carries a 'Material uncertainty related to going concern' paragraph -- it was NOT lifted despite the NZ$4.2m cash. Note 2 conditions the going-concern basis on (a) targeted revenue growth from the existing portfolio, (b) a disciplined cost structure and (c) FreightAI delivery within the Board's cost envelope, and states that a material overrun in the next 12 months 'could place pressure on the Group's available liquidity'. No FreightAI revenue is assumed by the Board until H2 FY28.

MOVED GOALPOSTS: annual EBITDA breakeven was guided for FY26, deferred to FY27 in Nov-2025, and the FY27 guidance is now 'approaching' breakeven. The base case does NOT reach EBITDA breakeven (pre-SBC) until FY28 and stays below management's FY27 trajectory: year-1 revenue growth 13% is the floor of the 13-18% guide (Q1 FY27 printed +18% revenue / +17% ARR), year-1 pre-SBC EBITDA margin -5% (about -0.55m) vs 'approaching breakeven'.

MANAGEMENT CHANGE: CEO AJ Smith resigned 19-Apr-2026 (left the board 11-Jun-2026); Dewald van Rensburg appointed CEO 15-Jun-2026. The company announced on 20-Aug-2026 that it will seek a PRIMARY ASX listing (no application lodged yet) and appointed two Australian directors. A primary ASX listing is usually the precursor to a further Australian raise -- consistent with the funding gap below.

FUNDING GAP (base case, no new raise): cumulative owner FCF is negative through FY29 and net cash troughs at the level shown in sanity_check.cash_runway; the base case therefore implies at least one more equity raise or a cut to FreightAI spend. The DCF discounts the negative flows, which is equivalent to assuming the shortfall is funded at fair value. sanity_check.dilution_at_current_price shows the per-share value if the shortfall plus a NZ$1m buffer were instead raised at today's NZ$0.117.

BEAR CASE HITS THE ZERO FLOOR: terminal-year owner FCF is negative, so the terminal value is floored at zero and the equity value is net cash less the PV of ten years of burn. The negative per-share figure is the house convention (SML.NZ, GEN.NZ, AGL.NZ); under limited liability existing holders' floor is zero, which is what the bear case is saying -- the business does not survive that path without a rescue raise that leaves current holders with very little.

DATA QUALITY: (1) Metrics.csv SharesOutstanding 127.7m is the FY2025 WEIGHTED AVERAGE and is stale -- 36.4m shares (28%) have been issued since; the live NZX count is used here. (2) Metrics.csv StockBasedComp is the reserve balance, not the expense (see sbc_source). (3) The H1 FY2026 extract is a 3-page market release with no balance sheet. (4) The FY26 Annual Report PDF as lodged is font-corrupt (pdftotext returns zero digits); the corrected re-lodgement of 17-Jul-2026 extracts cleanly and was used. Recommend the financial-parser backfill FY2026 into core_metrics from it.

PRICE is a regular-session NZX trade (Friday 18-Sep-2026 15:47 NZST), not an after-hours print; the stock is 70% below its NZ$0.385 52-week high and trades a few thousand dollars a day, so the quote can move several percent on a single order.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 guidance floor (13-18% trading revenue growth), deliberately below the 25% three-year revenue CAGR and the 24.8% three-year ARR CAGR because of the breakeven-guidance slippage history
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-7.9% 3yr) is negative and the 5yr figure (+29%) is pure capital raising, not retained earnings -- neither is a growth signal for a loss-maker. EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative throughout). Revenue/ARR CAGR is the only meaningful history and it is being decelerated by guidance.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF history uses reported FCF less SBC expense (reserve movement for FY21-FY24 where the expense line was not extracted), interest income and lease cash. SBC is immaterial at every point, so the owner and reported series tell the same story: cash burn peaked at NZ$11.4m in FY2023 and has narrowed every year since to NZ$2.1m in FY2026 -- but it has never been positive.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue grows 13% in FY27 (floor of guidance; Q1 printed +18%) decelerating to 4% by FY36, driven by ARPC expansion (shipper ARPC +20-22%/yr on re-pricing and module cross-sell) against a flat-to-declining customer count. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin moves from -12.6% to -5% in FY27 -- i.e. management's 'approaching breakeven' slips again by roughly a year -- reaching breakeven in FY28 and 22% by FY36 as the 60-63% gross margin scales over a cost base held near NZ$11m. FreightAI is delivered (capex 15% of revenue in FY27, 11% FY28) but contributes only modestly. Cumulative burn exhausts net cash around FY29, so one more raise or a spend cut is implied.
scenario_narratives.bull: FreightAI ships on schedule (Sept-2027), lands mid-market freight forwarders currently on WiseTech/legacy systems, and the primary ASX listing brings Australian institutional capital at a premium to today's price. Revenue growth holds 17-18% for three years (ARR already compounding 17%), pre-SBC EBITDA reaches breakeven in FY28 and 28% by FY35 -- still below the 30%+ mature margins of scaled trade-software peers. Terminal growth 3.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Retention slips back toward the 87% seen in FY25 as re-pricing pushes small customers out, FreightAI overruns the Board's cost envelope (the going-concern note's stated trigger), Australian growth stalls against WiseTech, and the company cannot raise on acceptable terms in a thin small-cap market (as in 2023 when it reached 27% of target). Revenue growth fades to 2-3%, EBITDA never clears 3% pre-SBC, owner FCF stays negative every year, the terminal value floors at zero and the equity is worth net cash less the burn -- negative: the business does not survive this path without a rescue raise.

entry_price.method: 15% IRR: PV of ten years of owner FCF at 15% + PV of a terminal value BUILT AT 15% (min(Gordon@15%, 15x FCF_10), floored at zero) + net cash, per fully diluted share; computed per scenario and probability-weighted. No lower-cost exit buyer is assumed.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at its own rate; the 14% row equals valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the 15% row equals entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; base-case drivers; TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 15x))

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% (house default 15%) because the FY26 audit opinion still carries a going-concern material uncertainty, the base case itself implies another raise, EBITDA-breakeven guidance has slipped twice, and the CEO changed in mid-2026. Bull cut to 20% (default 35%) because it needs three independent things to go right: FreightAI delivered on time and cost, adoption against a far better-capitalised incumbent, and an ASX raise at a premium. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: band_position set to null: SBC is ~1% of revenue so the house/street band is only NZ$0.007 wide and the NZ$0.117 price sits far outside it (raw reading ~940%). The band collapsed -- the valuation does not depend on SBC treatment; the price is above even the street bull-weighted figure.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF basis: SBC expensed, interest income stripped, leases charged in the flows, capitalised development treated as capex, terminal value the lower of Gordon and 15x and floored at zero, share count flat at the live fully diluted figure.
key_judgments: Base case sits below management's own FY27 guidance on both growth and margin because of the two prior breakeven slips.
Bear weight 30% for the unresolved going-concern paragraph.
No credit for FreightAI revenue beyond what ARPC expansion already implies; the Board's own forecast assumes none until H2 FY28.

methodology: Component-built owner-FCF DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2027E-FY2036E), end-of-year discounting at a 14% NZD cost of equity, terminal value = max(0, min(Gordon, 15x FCF_10)), net cash added, fully diluted 164.14m shares. Entry price at a 15% hurdle with the terminal value rebuilt at 15%. Reference: .claude/skills/dcf-methods/references/owner-fcf.md sections 1-7.
